title: 'American Horror Story' Finale: Paul Anthony Kelly on the Season 13 Ending and Whether He'll Return
text: ‘American Horror Story’ Finale: Paul Anthony Kelly on the Season 13 Ending and Whether He’ll Return The 'Love Story' star speaks with THR about playing young Mr. Nas and his reaction to this season's conclusion: 'I was flabbergasted.' Throughout the season, the witches have been doing everything in their power to defeat young Mr. Nas is Satan’s son and that Constance Langdon and Fiona Goode are twin sisters and daughters of Satan and Sister Jude , the stakes reach their highest point in Thursday’s finale. 'Snowfall' Spinoff Boss Malcolm Spellman Lays Out Multi-Season Plan for 'The Drop,' Why Season One Was Just a \"Dash of What's Coming\" In the concluding episode, young Mr. Nas kills his medical specialist, Mr. Phibes , as well as the older version of himself. Meanwhile, Fiona introduces Constance to the basics of witchcraft, hinting at her potential place within the Coven.Ben and Madison’s romance also takes an unexpected turn when, immediately after the two have sex, Madison becomes pregnant and gives birth to their daughter. When the newborn appears to be dead, young Mr. Nas brings the baby back to life. But the witches aren’t done fighting. After Mallory travels through time once again, she and Cordelia realize what they must do to save the world: convince Ben to sacrifice himself.Ben ultimately agrees and stabs himself in the heart with a sword, turning to ashes and defeating Satan. Young Mr. Nas is left trapped inside The Last Supper painting — a fate Constance foreshadowed during her first meeting with Ben in the, working alongside Lange, his character’s fate and whether he’d be interested in returning — or thinks Mr. Nas could return — for the already-renewed 14th season of When you first signed on for the season, did you know what your character’s ending would be, or when did you find out?Oh, boy. I didn’t really know anything about how the season would go. They were writing it as we went along. I think there were maybe five episodes when I started, and there are 13 episodes in the season, so things change, things go and just play along.., perhaps. I don’t know. I’m pretty busy at home with the baby, so my TV time doesn’t really exist anymore. I get to work on TV but not watch it. I think maybe it’s more of a purgatory situation. I mean, he’s stuck in the painting, being overwatched by the Coven. For as long as he’s stuck in there, who’s to say? Maybe season 18 will be the rise of young Mr. Nas again.Nope. I don’t think anybody knows a true answer on that. It needs to be written. Tango dancing with Jessica Lange.That was definitely a high point for me. What was it like filming some of the death scenes where your character has to kill people? It was a lot of fun. I mean, the prosthetic work was incredible.The effects, the blood splattering — especially when my character, young Mr. Nas, has to kill the old version of Mr. Nas — got gory. There was a lot of that black goo; it got everywhere. It was actually a little bit of a mishap and sprayed me down. It wasn’t supposed to, but it was a lot of fun. Who knows with Ryan Murphy?He’s always bringing things back and new twists and tales. It’s very possible. If I get the call, then yeah, I would seriously consider it. Yeah, but I have no idea.Who knows what’s in store. This is your first time working in the horror genre as well. Is that a genre that you hope to continue in?‘Nocturne’ Review: Liev Schreiber and Stephen Graham Get Handcuffed by Clichés in Apple’s Dully Competent Serial Killer ThrillerThe Hollywood Reporter is a part of PMX Global, LLC, a subsidiary of Penske Media Corporation. © 2026 The Hollywood Reporter, LLC.
